blocks.text: I then explained everything to Murray and asked him to show me what had already been written.
After seeing it, I said that the truth of the Khalsa had not been stated there. (27)
So Murray, now friendly toward me, called me again and said: write down for me how the Khalsa came into being. (28)
I replied: you are a man of understanding; Hindus and Muslims have been at variance from the beginning, and each abuses the other. (29)
Then Captain Murray answered that the English were skilled at separating truth from falsehood, like a swan distinguishing milk from water, and that he wished only the truth to be written. (30–31)
